title: security-audit findings.json
description: Contract of <project>/02-DOCS/security/audit-<YYYY-MM-DD>/findings.json. Documentation only: scripts/validate-findings.mjs enforces these rules by hand (no ajv) and adds the disk checks a schema cannot express — cited files and lines exist under project_root, evidence files exist non-empty under evidence/ or fixes/ of the audit dir, no '..'/absolute/symlink escapes, coverage cross-references resolve, 'complete' runs reviewed something and left nothing unreviewed, tool_path is a real 01-TOOLS/security/<platform>/ dir with a README.md and a check, no likely live secret in any key or string of findings.json nor in any file of the audit dir (report.html and scratch/ excepted; symlinks refused; files over 2 MB refused), findings.json <= 5 MB, cited project files <= 5 MB, nesting <= 32.

project_root.description: Absolute path of the audited project; must be an existing directory. Every locations[].path is relative to it.

scope.description: Free-form description of what was in scope (paths, platforms, exclusions).

status.description: 'complete' is refused while any coverage unit is not done or any platform is not reviewed, and when there are no units and no platforms at all.

partial_reason.description: Why the run is partial. Required when status is partial.

findings.description: Every candidate examined, including rejected ones.

units.description: What was (and was not) reviewed. Every confirmed or needs_validation finding must be referenced by at least one unit; every referenced id must exist.

platforms.description: Platforms the project uses (GitHub, Vercel, Postgres, Hetzner...).

user_actions.description: Things only the user can do (rotate a key, click a setting).

relPath.description: Relative path: no leading '/', no drive letter, no '..' segment, no symlink on the way, must resolve to a regular file inside its base.

verdict.description: confirmed = proven by an artifact or command output on disk; needs_validation = plausible, one named fact missing; rejected = ruled out.

platform.description: Platform name. Required when surface is platform.

class.description: Attack class id (e.g. idor, sqli, ssrf).

principal.description: Who can trigger it. Required unless rejected.

boundary.description: Trust boundary crossed. Required unless rejected.

locations.description: Where the finding lives. Code: a file and line range, and a confirmed or needs_validation code finding needs at least one (line_start <= line_end <= the file's line count). Platform: the resource the setting was read from, e.g. hetzner:server/app-01/firewall.

evidence.description: Evidence files inside the audit dir. A confirmed finding needs at least one of kind artifact or command_output; files must exist and be non-empty, and must contain no live secret.

path.description: Relative to the audit dir, under evidence/ or fixes/ (never findings.json, ledger.json or report.html).

missing_evidence.description: The exact fact still missing. Required for needs_validation.

rejection_reason.description: Why it was ruled out. Required for rejected.

rollback.description: How to undo the fix. Required when status is applied or rolled_back.

artifact.description: Recheck output, relative to the audit dir, under evidence/ or fixes/. Required when result is pass or fail; checked whenever present.

manual_steps.description: Steps the user must do by hand; shown in 'Your steps' while the finding is open.

findings.description: Ids of findings this unit produced; each must exist.

detected_by.description: What revealed it (a config file, a dependency).

tool_path.description: Tool used to review it: 01-TOOLS/security/<platform>/, relative to project_root. Must be a real directory (no symlink anywhere on the way) holding a README.md and at least one other regular file. Required when reviewed.
